citations.title: E-commerce grievance officer: acknowledge in 48 hours, resolve in one month
citations.plain: Every e-commerce platform must have a grievance officer. That officer must acknowledge your complaint within 48 hours and resolve it within one month of receiving it. Sellers on marketplaces must also appoint a grievance officer with the same timelines (rule 6(4)(b)).

citations.title: Seller/platform cannot refuse return or refund for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods
citations.plain: A seller on a marketplace (rule 6(3)) and an inventory e-commerce entity (rule 7(4)) cannot refuse to take back goods or refuse a refund if the goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or not as advertised. The same applies if delivery was late, unless the delay was due to force majeure.

citations.title: Reliefs the District Commission can order
citations.plain: If your complaint is proved, the Commission can order the seller or service provider to remove defects, replace the goods, refund the price or charges with interest, pay compensation for loss or injury (including punitive damages), stop the unfair practice, withdraw hazardous goods, issue corrective advertisements, and pay your costs.

deadlines.note: Acknowledgement is due within 48 hours. This is the company's deadline, not yours.

COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 35 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. That I am a consumer as defined under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, having purchased a phone for Rs 18,499 from the Opposite Party's online platform (Order ID: OD12345).

2. That the phone was returned to the Opposite Party, and the pickup was successfully completed on 10 September 2026.

3. That despite the return of the product, the Opposite Party has failed to process the refund of Rs 18,499. The Opposite Party has repeatedly informed me that the refund is 'under process'.

4. That I have raised 4 separate complaint tickets with the Opposite Party regarding this delay, with the last ticket raised on 01 October 2026. Despite these efforts, the refund remains pending.

5. That the failure to refund the amount for the returned product constitutes a deficiency in service under Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and an unfair trade practice under Section 2(47) of the Act.

6. That the Opposite Party is obligated under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, to process refunds for returned goods in a timely manner.

7. That this Commission has the jurisdiction to entertain this complaint as I reside in [[FILL: Jaipur]] and the amount paid is within the pecuniary jurisdiction of this District Commission.

8. That this complaint is filed within the limitation period of two years as prescribed under Section 69 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

RELIEFS PRAYED:

In view of the facts stated above, it is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Commission may be pleased to direct the Opposite Party to:

a) Refund the amount of Rs 18,499 along with interest at the rate of 18% per annum from the date of pickup (10 September 2026) until the date of actual payment;

b) Pay compensation for the mental agony and harassment caused by the deficiency in service;

c) Pay the costs of this litigation.

citations.title: Who is a 'consumer'
citations.plain: You are a consumer if you buy goods or hire/avail a service for payment (paid, promised, or in instalments), including online, teleshopping, direct selling or multi-level marketing. People who use the goods or service with the buyer's approval are also covered. Buying for resale or a commercial purpose is excluded, but buying something to earn your own livelihood through self-employment is not treated as commercial.

citations.title: Meaning of 'deficiency' in service
citations.plain: A deficiency is any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature or manner of a service that the law or a contract requires. It also covers negligence or acts or omissions that cause you loss, and deliberately withholding relevant information from you.

citations.title: Meaning of 'unfair trade practice'
citations.plain: An unfair trade practice is any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice used to promote the sale, use or supply of goods or services. Examples listed in the Act include false claims about standard, quality, quantity or grade of goods (oral, written, visual or electronic).

citations.title: Who can file a complaint, and electronic filing
citations.plain: A complaint can be filed with the District Commission by the consumer, by a registered consumer association, by one or more consumers on behalf of many with the same interest (with the Commission's permission), or by the Central/State Government or the Central Authority. The Act allows complaints to be filed electronically, and the prescribed fee can be paid electronically.

citations.title: Limitation period for filing complaint
citations.plain: You must file a consumer complaint within two years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose. A later complaint can still be accepted if you show sufficient cause for the delay, but the Commission must record its reasons for condoning the delay.

citations.title: E-commerce refunds must be paid within a reasonable time
citations.plain: Once a refund request is accepted, the platform must pay it within a reasonable time, or within the time set by RBI or other applicable law. The rules do not fix a specific number of days.

citations.title: Seller/platform cannot refuse return or refund for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods
citations.plain: A seller on a marketplace (rule 6(3)) and an inventory e-commerce entity (rule 7(4)) cannot refuse to take back goods or refuse a refund if the goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or not as advertised. The same applies if delivery was late, unless the delay was due to force majeure.

send_instructions: Register and log in to the e-Jagriti portal (https://e-jagriti.gov.in/) to file your complaint electronically.
Upload the draft document (saved as a PDF) along with copies of your order invoice, pickup confirmation, and screenshots of your complaint tickets.
Since the amount paid is Rs 18,499, there is no filing fee required as per Rule 7 of the Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020.
Keep a digital copy of the filed complaint and the acknowledgment receipt generated by the portal for your records.
If you need assistance with the e-filing process, you can call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for guidance.
